overview: This event ties together ocf recovery procedures, contact unusual attitudes, and all aerobatic maneuvers in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: OCF Recovery Procedures is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.

children.text: Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Aircraft is unresponsive to normal control inputs
Caused by a stalled condition where inertial forces exceed aerodynamic control authority
Controls may feel ineffective or act in reverse
Failing to reduce power/deploy speed brake
Use ~4 Gs to smoothly recover to level flight
As airspeed/Gs increase (~4 Gs), perform AGSM
Raise nose to ~10° pitch.

items.text: recovery from NH, NL, or Inverted attitudes due to disorientation, misflown maneuvers, or external factors. Recovery is visual (VFR) and must be completed above 6000’ AGL

children.text: PCL - MAX (if low airspeed)
Use back stick to bring nose to horizon
Roll upright as nose approaches horizon
Roll wings level, raise nose, check oil pressure, power as req.

items.text: All Aerobatic Maneuvers is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.

The usual trap is missing the setup picture, then trying to salvage All Aerobatic Maneuvers late.
